NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), City Council Resolution Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493,
  2498, 2499, 2503, and 2505, due to the continuing state of emergency, including masking and social
  distancing directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus, this meeting is being broadcast via
  teleconference. Members of the public may participate in-person in the Council Chambers, or virtually in
  the meeting in the following ways:

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1 669 900 6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 821 9936 4053 Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 821 9936 4053, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MAY 10, 2022

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City Hall and remotely
via teleconference, in accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361) and City Council
Resolution Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493, 2498, 2499, 2503 and 2505, due to the continuing
state of emergency, including masking and social distancing directives as a result of the
threat of the COVID-19 virus.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Boy Scout Troop 191.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  Zerunyan

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit

4.  CEREMONIAL

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING MAY 2022 “MENTAL HEALTH AWARENESS
  MONTH”

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF presented a Proclamation declaring May 2022 as Mental Health
Awareness Month.

B.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING MAY 2022 “MATERNAL MENTAL HEALTH
  AWARENESS MONTH”

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF presented a Proclamation declaring May 2022 as Maternal Mental
Health Awareness Month.

C.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING MAY 21, 2022 “NATIONAL KIDS TO PARKS DAY”

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF presented a Proclamation declaring May 21, 2022 as National
Kids to Parks Day.

D.  CERTIFICATE OF RECOGNITION – TOM JUDGE

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF presented a Certificate of Recognition to resident Tom Judge.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-H AS FOLLOWS BY
  THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
MAY 10, 2022
   AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF APRIL & MAY 2022

  APPROVED WARRANTS 65036 THROUGH 65068 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $48,268.44; AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 040422 THROUGH 040622
  IN THE AMOUNT OF $82,042.51; FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF
  $130,310.95 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF MARCH 12, 2022

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

D.  SPECIAL CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF APRIL 26, 2022

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

E.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF APRIL 26, 2022

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

F.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF APRIL 18, 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

G.  EQUESTRIAN MINUTES OF MARCH 28, 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

H.  SOUTH BAY CITIES COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS MEETING SUMMARY OF
  APRIL 28, 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Public comment received from Pastor Dan Burgoyne of Rolling Hills Covenant Church (RHCC),
as well as Donna Artino and Bill Reichert, who spoke against the April 26, 2022 City Council
decision granting an extension of the Special Use Permit for RHCC for the requested time of
three months, while prohibiting the amplification of music, and with no further extensions for
the existing permit. Comments also received from resident Bridget Carman, in support of the
City Council’s decision for the RHCC Permit.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

None.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  NON-PROFIT GRANT PROGRAM

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the non-profit grant program
  guidelines to be implemented this fiscal year in the budgeted amount of $20,000 and
  each subsequent year that the City budgets for the program.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
MAY 10, 2022
 COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA inquired how many non-profits within Rolling Hills Estates
would qualify under the outlined criteria, noting that if a small number of applications are
received, the grant amount could potentially be increased. Assistant City Manager Davis
confirmed the grant amount could be increased, and also noted that the grant will return for
a second round next year.

Assistant City Manager Davis explained that funds will be awarded upon the deadline, in
response to COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN inquired if churches could apply if they had less than 50
employees. Assistant City Manager Davis and City Attorney Davis stated that it would
depend, and that staff would look into this.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No additional public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZUCKERMAN, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  APPROVE THE NON-PROFIT GRANT PROGRAM GUIDELINES TO BE
  IMPLEMENTED THIS FISCAL YEAR IN THE BUDGETED AMOUNT OF
  $20,000 AND EACH SUBSEQUENT YEAR THAT THE CITY BUDGETS FOR
  THE PROGRAM.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

B.  LEGISLATIVE UPDATE

  Recommendation: That the City Council endorse the various positions listed and
  authorize the Mayor or City Manager to communicate the City’s position when and
  where appropriate.

City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ expressed concern about approving all listed bills as a whole
without a deeper understanding of each bill as it relates to the City.

Discussion ensued about the proposed recommendation as compared to the current process
the City follows.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZUCKERMAN, AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  RECEIVE AND FILE THE REPORT AND DIRECT STAFF TO CONTINUE
  WITH ITS CURRENT PROCESS OF HAVING THE CITY MANAGER OR
  MAYOR COMMUNICATE THE CITY’S POSITION ON LEGISLATIVE BILLS
  WHEN AND WHERE APPROPRIATE.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

C.  SOUTH BAY REGIONAL HOUSING TRUST LEGISLATION

  Recommendation: That the City Council support the concept for state legislation
  requested by the South Bay Cities Council of Governments’ (SBCCOG) Board of

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MAY 10, 2022
   Directors that would create a South Bay Regional Housing Trust, including a state
  budget request for seed funding.

City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ thanked the SBCCOG for coming up with this creative solution.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZUCKERMAN, AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  CONSENSUS OF THE CITY COUNCIL TO SUPPORT THE CONCEPT FOR
  STATE LEGISLATION REQUESTED BY THE SOUTH BAY CITIES COUNCIL
  OF GOVERNMENTS’ (SBCCOG) BOARD OF DIRECTORS THAT WOULD
  CREATE A SOUTH BAY REGIONAL HOUSING TRUST, INCLUDING A
  STATE BUDGET REQUEST FOR SEED FUNDING.

  AYES:  Huff, Stegura, Schmitz and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER AND STATUS OF
  CITY EVENTS (VERBAL REPORT)

City Manager Grammer reported that there have been no changes to the Los Angeles County
Health Officer Order since the last City Council meeting, and restated that masks are currently
required for all public transit. The number of COVID cases has increased over the last several
weeks due to the new subvariants, but hospitalizations and deaths continue to decrease.
Lastly, the second booster shot is available to those 50 years and older or for those who are
immunocompromised.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

City Attorney Davis reported that he presented a draft sign code update to the Planning
Commission on May 9, which will next be presented to the City Council as a public hearing for
introduction and first reading on May 24.

City Attorney Davis requested agendizing as a subsequent need item, a closed session this
evening pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2); significant exposure to litigation,
in response to a letter threatening litigation received earlier that evening from Advocates for
Faith and Freedom signed by Robert Tyler on behalf of Rolling Hills Covenant Church.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADD AS A “SUBSEQUENT NEED” ITEM, A CLOSED SESSION PURSUANT
  TO SUBDIVISION (D)(2) OF CALIFORNIA GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION
  54956.9 FOR CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – SIGNIFICANT
  EXPOSURE TO LITIGATION, (1) AS THE ITEM AROSE AFTER THE
  POSTING OF THE AGENDA, NECESSITATING THE CITY COUNCIL'S
  IMMEDIATE CONSIDERATION AND/OR ACTION.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF attended the Southern California Association of Governments
(SCAG) General Assembly last weekend as the City’s delegate.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MAY 10, 2022
 MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF will attend the Board of Directors meeting this Friday and Saturday
in Sacramento for the League of California Cities (Cal Cities).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA attended the League of California Cities Community Services
meeting on April 28.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

NONE.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

**CLOSED SESSION ITEM ADDED AFTER POSTING OF AGENDA**

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2)
  Title: Significant exposure to litigation

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 8:45 p.m. MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF adjourned the City Council meeting to the next
regular City Council meeting on Tuesday, May 24, 2022, at 7:00 pm for the purpose of a
Regular meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Britt Huff
City Clerk  Mayor Pro Tem

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
MAY 10, 2022
